title: BIM solved geometric coordination; documentation workflows remain the manual bottleneck
content:
An industry vendor's framing of the post-BIM gap (BIM Services LLC, Mar 2026) — independently corroborating the practitioner diagnosis from DT BAU:

BIM has been instrumental in creating structured digital environments, but it primarily addresses **geometric and coordination challenges** (visualization, clash detection, design handoff). Documentation workflows stay largely manual:

- Professionals manage massive technical documents, often **1000+ pages**: submittals, transmittals, RFIs (Requests for Information), compliance documents, project approvals
- Heavy reliance on manual data entry and interpretation
- Limited integration between models and textual/compliance-based data
- Fragmented workflows between BIM models and supporting documents
- Repetitive, error-prone administrative tasks divert skilled professionals from decision-making, on-site problem-solving, and coordination

The stated conclusion: to "work smarter," the industry must extend BIM into intelligent, **document-aware ecosystems** — the same layer above 3D models that Powerhouse's construction positioning targets. Notably, the article dismisses the usual sensors/drones framing of construction AI in favor of "making sense of messy, unstructured data like specs and contracts" — cognitive automation over field automation.
description: Industry-vendor corroboration: despite BIM, 1000+ page documents (submittals, RFIs, compliance, approvals) dominate construction time — BIM never integrated textual/compliance data.
